nodes.label: Sun
nodes.definition: Sites that receive six or more hours of direct sun in summer.

nodes.label: Shade
nodes.definition: Sites with little or no direct sun: filtered light under a canopy or deep shade on the north side of buildings and under dense trees.

nodes.label: Part shade
nodes.definition: Sites with roughly three to six hours of direct sun, or sun for only part of the day.

nodes.label: Full sun
nodes.definition: Six or more hours of direct sun in summer; no overhead canopy.

nodes.label: Full sun only if soil kept moist
nodes.definition: Takes full sun only where the soil does not dry out; in dry sun it scorches or stalls.

nodes.label: Part sun/part shade
nodes.definition: Three to six hours of direct sun, or dappled light for much of the day.

nodes.label: Filtered shade
nodes.definition: Light reaching the plant through a tree canopy or lattice all day; bright but never direct for long.

nodes.label: Deep shade
nodes.definition: Less than about two hours of direct sun; under dense canopy or on the north side of buildings.

nodes.label: Sheltered
nodes.definition: A position protected from strong or cold wind, for example near a wall or inside a planting.

nodes.label: Acidic
nodes.definition: Soil with pH below about 6.5, typical of coastal BC under conifers.

nodes.label: Alkaline
nodes.definition: Soil with pH above about 7.5, usually over limestone or where lime has been added.

nodes.label: Bog
nodes.definition: Permanently wet, peaty, acidic ground with standing water close to the surface.

nodes.label: Humus rich
nodes.definition: Dark soil high in decomposed organic matter; holds moisture and nutrients well.

nodes.label: Rocky or gravelly or dry
nodes.definition: Thin, stony or sandy ground that drains fast and holds little water or nutrient.

nodes.label: Well-drained
nodes.definition: Soil through which water passes freely, so roots are never left standing in water.

nodes.label: dry
nodes.definition: Little available soil moisture for long periods; relies on rain or drought tolerance.

nodes.label: average
nodes.definition: Ordinary garden moisture: rain plus occasional watering, neither dry nor wet for long.

nodes.label: moist
nodes.definition: Soil that stays damp but not waterlogged, such as a shaded bed or a slope base.

nodes.label: wet
nodes.definition: Soil often saturated: pond margins, ditches, poorly drained low ground.

nodes.label: wide range
nodes.definition: Tolerates anything from dry to wet once established.

nodes.label: Gaultheria
nodes.definition: The genus Gaultheria, read from the scientific name; family Ericaceae.

nodes.label: Vaccinium
nodes.definition: The genus Vaccinium, read from the scientific name; family Ericaceae.

nodes.label: Canopy
nodes.definition: The uppermost layer: tree crowns that form the roof of a planting and shade everything beneath.
nodes.source_of_term: Robinson, N. (2016) The Planting Design Handbook, 3rd ed., Routledge, ch. 8 'Forest Structures' / 'Typical Canopy Structures as Models for Design' (tree canopy)

nodes.label: Understory
nodes.definition: Small trees and large shrubs that grow beneath the canopy and above the shrub layer (Robinson's low tree canopy / sub-canopy).
nodes.source_of_term: Robinson, N. (2016) The Planting Design Handbook, 3rd ed., Routledge, ch. 8 (two- and three-layer canopy structures: 'low tree canopy')

nodes.label: Shrub layer
nodes.definition: Woody plants branching from near the ground that fill the space between the ground layer and the trees.
nodes.source_of_term: Robinson, N. (2016) The Planting Design Handbook, 3rd ed., Routledge, ch. 8 ('shrub and sapling layer' in the canopy-structure types)

nodes.label: Ground layer
nodes.definition: The lowest layer: herbaceous, carpeting and low woody plants that cover the soil.
nodes.source_of_term: Robinson, N. (2016) The Planting Design Handbook, 3rd ed., Routledge, ch. 8 ('herb layer' / ground cover principle) and ch. 3 'Ground-level Planting (Carpeting Plants)'

nodes.label: Ground-level planting (carpeting)
nodes.definition: Carpeting plants at ground level. Bounds are approximate readings of the heading names (knee ≈ 0.5 m, eye ≈ 1.6 m) — to confirm against the chapter text.
nodes.source_of_term: Robinson, N. (2016) The Planting Design Handbook, 3rd ed., Routledge, ch. 3 'Spatial Characteristics of Plants' (section headings)

nodes.label: Low planting (below knee)
nodes.definition: Shrubs and herbaceous plants below knee height. Bounds are approximate readings of the heading names (knee ≈ 0.5 m, eye ≈ 1.6 m) — to confirm against the chapter text.
nodes.source_of_term: Robinson, N. (2016) The Planting Design Handbook, 3rd ed., Routledge, ch. 3 'Spatial Characteristics of Plants' (section headings)

nodes.label: Medium-height planting (knee to eye level)
nodes.definition: Planting between knee and eye level: a physical barrier that still allows views over it. Bounds are approximate readings of the heading names (knee ≈ 0.5 m, eye ≈ 1.6 m) — to confirm against the chapter text.
nodes.source_of_term: Robinson, N. (2016) The Planting Design Handbook, 3rd ed., Routledge, ch. 3 'Spatial Characteristics of Plants' (section headings)

nodes.label: Tall shrub planting (above eye level)
nodes.definition: Planting above eye level: visual enclosure and screening. Bounds are approximate readings of the heading names (knee ≈ 0.5 m, eye ≈ 1.6 m) — to confirm against the chapter text.
nodes.source_of_term: Robinson, N. (2016) The Planting Design Handbook, 3rd ed., Routledge, ch. 3 'Spatial Characteristics of Plants' (section headings)

nodes.label: Tree planting
nodes.definition: Trees: canopy, ceiling and shade above head height. Bounds are approximate readings of the heading names (knee ≈ 0.5 m, eye ≈ 1.6 m) — to confirm against the chapter text.
nodes.source_of_term: Robinson, N. (2016) The Planting Design Handbook, 3rd ed., Routledge, ch. 3 'Spatial Characteristics of Plants' (section headings)

nodes.label: Screen
nodes.definition: Planting that blocks a view: visual enclosure above eye level, opaque in the seasons it has to work.
nodes.source_of_term: Robinson, N. (2016) The Planting Design Handbook, 3rd ed., Routledge, ch. 3 'Planting Above Eye Level (Tall Shrub Planting)' and ch. 4 'Permeability and Transparency of Enclosure'

nodes.label: Scrim
nodes.definition: A partly transparent screen: planting open enough to be seen through, which filters a view rather than blocking it. Term from the brief; not found under this name in Robinson, whose nearest heading is 'Permeability and Transparency of Enclosure' — to confirm.
nodes.source_of_term: brief 2026-11-02; Robinson, N. (2016) The Planting Design Handbook, 3rd ed., Routledge, ch. 4 'Permeability and Transparency of Enclosure' (nearest documented concept)

nodes.label: Barrier
nodes.definition: Planting that stops movement: a dense, continuous physical enclosure, with or without a visual screen.
nodes.source_of_term: Robinson, N. (2016) The Planting Design Handbook, 3rd ed., Routledge, ch. 4 'Degree of Enclosure' (physical vs visual enclosure) and ch. 3 'Knee- to Eye-level Planting'

nodes.label: Ceiling
nodes.definition: Tree crowns forming an overhead plane that encloses a space from above.
nodes.source_of_term: Robinson, N. (2016) The Planting Design Handbook, 3rd ed., Routledge, ch. 3 'Tree Planting' and ch. 4 'Degree of Enclosure'

nodes.label: Matrix
nodes.definition: A continuous ground-covering planting of one or a few species into which structural and seasonal plants are set.
nodes.source_of_term: Oudolf, P. & Kingsbury, N. (2013) Planting: A New Perspective, Timber Press (matrix plants); Robinson, N. (2016) The Planting Design Handbook, 3rd ed., Routledge, ch. 8 'Matrix Planting'; Rainer, T. & West, C. (2015) Planting in a Post-Wild World, Timber Press (groundcover matrix layer)

nodes.label: Drift
nodes.definition: An elongated, irregular group of one species that flows through a planting.
nodes.source_of_term: Oudolf, P. & Kingsbury, N. (2013) Planting: A New Perspective, Timber Press (drifts, as against blocks)

nodes.label: Grouping
nodes.definition: Several plants of one kind set together as a block, group or mass.
nodes.source_of_term: Oudolf, P. & Kingsbury, N. (2013) Planting: A New Perspective, Timber Press (blocks); Robinson, N. (2016) The Planting Design Handbook, 3rd ed., Routledge, ch. 12 'Planting Patterns'; KPU 'Group or mass planting'

nodes.label: Scatter
nodes.definition: Single plants distributed through a planting at random to give a natural feel.
nodes.source_of_term: Oudolf, P. & Kingsbury, N. (2013) Planting: A New Perspective, Timber Press (scatter plants)

nodes.label: Layering
nodes.definition: Combining plants of different heights so that canopy, understorey, shrub and ground layers occupy the same ground.
nodes.source_of_term: Robinson, N. (2016) The Planting Design Handbook, 3rd ed., Routledge, ch. 8 'Layers Within Layers' and ch. 12 'Canopy and Seasonal Layers'; Rainer, T. & West, C. (2015) Planting in a Post-Wild World, Timber Press (vertical layers of a designed plant community)

nodes.label: Structural
nodes.definition: Long-lived plants that give a planting its year-round framework.
nodes.source_of_term: Rainer, T. & West, C. (2015) Planting in a Post-Wild World, Timber Press (structural and framework layer); Robinson, N. (2016) The Planting Design Handbook, 3rd ed., Routledge (structure planting)

nodes.label: Seasonal theme
nodes.definition: Plants that dominate the picture in one season and recede in others.
nodes.source_of_term: Rainer, T. & West, C. (2015) Planting in a Post-Wild World, Timber Press (seasonal theme layer); Robinson, N. (2016) The Planting Design Handbook, 3rd ed., Routledge, ch. 12 'Canopy and Seasonal Layers'

nodes.label: Ground cover
nodes.definition: Low plants that cover the soil between and beneath the others; the layer that carries most of the diversity and ecological function.
nodes.source_of_term: Rainer, T. & West, C. (2015) Planting in a Post-Wild World, Timber Press (ground cover layer); Robinson, N. (2016) The Planting Design Handbook, 3rd ed., Routledge, ch. 8 'Two Principles – Ground Cover and Diversity'

nodes.label: Filler
nodes.definition: Short-lived or fast plants that fill gaps while the framework establishes.
nodes.source_of_term: Rainer, T. & West, C. (2015) Planting in a Post-Wild World, Timber Press (dynamic filler layer); KPU 'Filler'

nodes.label: Accent
nodes.definition: A single plant placed for emphasis or focus: a specimen.
nodes.source_of_term: Robinson, N. (2016) The Planting Design Handbook, 3rd ed., Routledge, ch. 7 'Emphasis and Accent' and ch. 12 'Accents'; KPU 'Specimen plant', 'Accent plant'
